title: WBJEE 2026
body: West Bengal Joint Entrance Examinations Board (WBJEEB)
summary: WBJEEB conducts WBJEE for undergraduate Engineering, Technology, Pharmacy and Architecture seats in West Bengal universities, government colleges and self-financed institutes for the 2026-27 session.
eligibility: Class 12 or equivalent, with Physics and Mathematics plus the other subjects listed in the WBJEE-2026 information bulletin.
Age, domicile and minimum marks follow the bulletin. Rank alone does not guarantee a seat.
pattern: Pen-and-paper test answered on an OMR sheet.
Engineering papers cover Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics.
Negative marking applies as published in the information bulletin.
note: Fee depends on category and gender: General male ₹500, and lower slabs down to ₹200 for some reserved and third-gender categories. The fee is not refundable.

title: COMEDK UGET 2026
fullName: Consortium of Medical, Engineering and Dental Colleges of Karnataka — Undergraduate Entrance Test 2026
summary: COMEDK UGET is the computer-based test for B.E. and B.Tech seats in participating Karnataka engineering colleges. Medical and dental seats are filled through NEET, not COMEDK.
eligibility: Indian citizens, and OCI or PIO candidates, as notified by COMEDK.
Class 12 with Physics, Mathematics and English, plus Chemistry or Biotechnology or Biology or Computer Science or Electronics.
General merit needs at least 45% aggregate in PCM (40% for Karnataka SC, ST and OBC), with each of those subjects passed. All subjects must be from one board.
pattern: 180 multiple-choice questions: Physics 60, Chemistry 60, Mathematics 60.
One mark for each correct answer. No negative marking.
English only. The test was held on Saturday, 9 May 2026, in the slot printed on the Test Admission Ticket.
note: Registration fee is ₹1,950 plus payment-gateway charges. It is non-refundable. COMEDK and Uni-GAUGE fees are separate if you apply for both.

title: SRMJEEE 2026
body: SRM Institute of Science and Technology
summary: SRMJEEE is SRM’s entrance exam for B.Tech at SRM IST campuses in Kattankulathur, Ramapuram, Vadapalani, Tiruchirappalli and Delhi-NCR, and at SRM University, Sonepat and SRM University, Andhra Pradesh.
eligibility: Passed, or appearing in, the 10+2 examination.
SRM asks for a minimum 60% aggregate in Physics and Mathematics plus one of Chemistry, Biotechnology, Biology, Computer Science or the other subjects listed on its admissions page.
pattern: Remote-proctored online test taken from a desktop or laptop.
Three phases. A separate application and fee are required for each phase you attempt.
Campus, programme and specialisation are chosen at counselling, not locked in at application.
note: SRM marked the phase dates as tentative. The application fee is ₹1,400 per phase and is not refundable.

title: IEMJEE 2026
summary: IEMJEE is the entrance exam for engineering admission through the IEM Group. You can pick an online slot inside the published window, or sit the offline paper at a listed centre.
eligibility: Eligibility is the criteria published by IEM for the 2026 engineering cycle.
Confirm the latest subject and marks rules on the IEMJEE page before you apply.
pattern: Online slots: 12:00–2:00 PM and 2:30–4:30 PM, on any date from 8 December 2025 to 30 May 2026.
Offline paper: 3 April 2026, 11:00 AM–2:00 PM, at the centres listed by IEM.
IEM states there is no examination fee.
note: Online venues include IEM Salt Lake and UEM Kolkata. The offline paper is also held at centres outside Kolkata, as listed by IEM.

title: VITEEE 2026
summary: VITEEE is the entrance exam for undergraduate engineering programmes in the VIT group of institutions. VIT allows a candidate to appear only once. A second attempt can cancel the application.
eligibility: Eligibility is the B.Tech 2026-27 criteria published by VIT.
The application fee covers application and the later counselling step, and VIT states it is not refundable.
pattern: 125 multiple-choice questions in 2 hours 30 minutes.
Mathematics or Biology 40, Physics 35, Chemistry 35, Aptitude 10, English 5.
Four marks for a correct answer and minus one for a wrong answer. Unanswered questions score zero.
Question paper is in English. Centres are in India and abroad.

schedule.label: Application fee
schedule.value: ₹1,350 in India; about USD 90 for centres abroad

note: VIT published this exam window as tentative. The number of exam days can differ by test city.

title: JEE Main & Advanced 2026
summary: JEE Main is the national exam for B.E. / B.Tech, and qualifying it is required for JEE Advanced. NTA held JEE Main 2026 in two sessions. IIT Roorkee conducted JEE Advanced 2026 on 17 May 2026. Both Advanced papers are compulsory.
eligibility: JEE Main eligibility, attempt rules and qualifying criteria are those in the JEE (Main) 2026 information bulletin. Paper 1 is for B.E. / B.Tech.
JEE Advanced is only for candidates who qualify JEE Main and meet the attempt rules in the JEE (Advanced) 2026 information brochure.
pattern: JEE Main Paper 1 is a computer-based test in Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics. NTA uses the better of the two session scores, as set out in the bulletin.
JEE Advanced is a computer-based test. Paper 1 is 9:00–12:00 IST and Paper 2 is 2:30–5:30 IST. Appearing in both papers is compulsory.
note: JEE Main Paper 1 fee in India is ₹1,000 for a General male candidate, down to ₹500 for SC, ST, PwD and third-gender candidates, per session. JEE Advanced fee at centres in India is ₹3,200, and ₹1,600 for female candidates and for SC, ST and PwD candidates. Gateway charges are extra, and the Advanced fee is not refundable. Advanced registration and updates are on jeeadv.ac.in.

title: MHT-CET 2026
fullName: Maharashtra Health and Technical Common Entrance Test 2026
body: State Common Entrance Test Cell, Maharashtra
summary: MHT-CET is the Maharashtra computer-based test for B.E. / B.Tech and the other technical courses it covers. The PCM and PCB groups are separate papers. A candidate may sit one group or both, and may take one attempt or both. The better percentile is used when both attempts are taken.
eligibility: Engineering admission uses the PCM group. Subject and marks rules are those in the MHT-CET 2026 information brochure.
The group chosen on the form cannot be changed later, and marks from one group are not transferred to the other.
pattern: PCM: 150 multiple-choice questions in 180 minutes. Physics and Chemistry carry 1 mark each. Mathematics carries 2 marks. No negative marking.
The first 90 minutes are Physics and Chemistry. That group is then submitted, and Mathematics opens for the next 90 minutes.
Centres are in Maharashtra. The paper is in English, and Marathi or Urdu only if that medium was chosen on the form.

schedule.label: PCM fee, one attempt
schedule.value: ₹1,300 General / outside Maharashtra; ₹1,000 for notified Maharashtra reserved categories

note: These attempt windows are from the State CET Cell notice. The shift and the exact day are on the admit card. Both attempts cost ₹2,600 (General) or ₹2,000 (notified Maharashtra reserved categories). The fee is not refundable. Gateway charges are extra.

title: NEET UG 2026
summary: NEET (UG) is the single national entrance exam for MBBS, BDS and the other undergraduate medical courses it covers, including AYUSH and BVSc & AH as notified for 2026. NTA held it on 3 May 2026 from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM IST.
eligibility: Age, subjects and the minimum qualifying marks are those in the NEET (UG) 2026 information bulletin.
A NEET score is required for undergraduate medical and dental admission in India.
pattern: Pen-and-paper exam. Duration is 3 hours, from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM.
Eligible PwD / PwBD candidates with compensatory time could continue until 6:00 PM.
Physics, Chemistry and Biology.
Held in 551 cities in India and 14 cities abroad.
note: India-centre fee: General ₹1,700, General-EWS and OBC-NCL ₹1,600, SC / ST / PwBD / third gender ₹1,000. Centres outside India are higher. Processing charges and GST are extra.
